run.question:
We have an active P1 incident — the checkout service in our production-us-east-2
cluster is throwing 500 errors and customers cannot complete payments. Please
investigate the root cause using the app-260-prod-logs index.

report.summary: The named index app-260-prod-logs does contain data for the incident cluster production-us-east-2, and that is the evidence used here: 8 of its 10 documents are us-east-2 records from checkout-service and payment-service on 2026-11-23 between 14:22:58Z and 17:17:58Z. Those records show a chain that starts outside the services: checkout-service 500s are attributed to the payment provider (30s timeout, 502 Bad Gateway) and to payment-service's failure rate tripping a circuit breaker, while payment-service's own failures are 30s timeouts calling the external provider stripe-us /v1/charges plus an acknowledged Stripe-US degraded mode with a retry queue depth of 1031. The deepest failing dependency the log evidence names is the external provider stripe-us; both internal services are the propagation path. Two hard limits remain: Kubernetes access in this Run covers only production-eu-west-2 (whose otel-demo checkout/payment deployments and pods are ready with 0 restarts, and whose flagd feature flags are all defaultVariant off), so no pod, event, ConfigMap or flag state for production-us-east-2 could be read; and Prometheus and Jaeger both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every attempt, so no error-rate, latency or span corroboration exists and those signals are unknown, not zero. The conclusion is therefore partial: the observed failure chain is well evidenced in logs, but the provider-side fault itself and any us-east-2 configuration (timeouts, breaker threshold, fault-injection flags) could not be verified.

claims.text: The app-260-prod-logs index in the registered Elasticsearch source (target m0-otel-20260909) is the only index present and holds 10 documents inside the authorized window; aggregations over those 10 documents give cluster=production-us-east-2 8 documents and cluster=production-eu-west-2 2 documents, service=checkout-service 6 and payment-service 4, level=ERROR 6 / WARN 2 / INFO 2, status_code 500:4, 504:2, 200:4.

In cluster production-us-east-2 / region us-east-2, checkout-service logged four ERROR status_code 500 lines for POST /api/checkout: 2026-11-23T15:22:58Z 'payment provider response timeout after 30s (provider=stripe-us)' (correlation_id chk-us-2142), 16:22:58Z 'circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41% > 25% threshold)' (chk-us-2208), 16:52:58Z 'payment provider returned 502 Bad Gateway' (chk-us-2252) and 17:17:58Z 'circuit-breaker open for payment-service' (chk-us-2280).

In cluster production-us-east-2 / region us-east-2, payment-service logged ERROR status_code 504 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms' at 2026-11-23T15:22:58Z (correlation_id chk-us-2142) and 16:37:58Z (chk-us-2220), and a WARN at 17:07:58Z 'Stripe-US degraded mode acknowledged via status page; retry queue depth=1031'.

The earliest deviation recorded for production-us-east-2 in the window is checkout-service WARN at 2026-11-23T14:22:58Z 'Latency on POST /api/checkout p95=1700ms (target 800ms)' (correlation_id chk-us-2001, status_code 200), about one hour before the first checkout 500.

The error texts place the failure upstream of both internal services: checkout-service's 500s are attributed to the payment provider (response timeout after 30s with provider=stripe-us, 'payment provider returned 502 Bad Gateway') and to payment-service's own failure rate (41%), while payment-service's own errors are 30s timeouts calling the external endpoint stripe-us /v1/charges and an acknowledged Stripe-US degraded mode, so the deepest failing dependency named in the evidence is the external provider stripe-us.

The two production-eu-west-2 documents in the same index show no failure in that cluster: checkout-service INFO 'Healthy: p95 latency 230ms over last 5 minutes' at 2026-11-23T15:22:58Z and payment-service INFO 'Stripe-EU responding normally, p95 latency 180ms' at 16:22:58Z. These are different-cluster entities and say nothing about production-us-east-2, but they rule out those eu-west-2 entities as affected.

In the Kubernetes cluster this Run can read (production-eu-west-2 scope, namespace otel-demo), all 24 deployments report ready/available replicas, including checkout 1/1 (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout) and payment 1/1 (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-payment), and all 22 pods are Running and ready with restartCount 0 and startTime 2026-11-23T14:36:29Z-14:38:04Z; this is not the incident cluster.

The flagd-config ConfigMap in otel-demo (readable cluster) defines fault-injection flags including paymentFailure ('Fail payment service charge requests n%'), paymentUnreachable ('Payment service is unavailable'), cartFailure, adFailure, adHighCpu, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad, and every one of them has defaultVariant 'off' with state ENABLED, i.e. no fault flag is switched on in that cluster.

Root cause is external provider degradation: stripe-us returned 502s and did not answer /v1/charges within 30s, payment-service consequently logged 504s and built a retry backlog (depth=1031), its failure rate reached 41% and tripped checkout-service's 25% circuit breaker, which produced the customer-facing 500s on POST /api/checkout. This is the chain the log texts record; the provider-side fault itself was not directly observed by any tool in this Run.

The 30s provider timeout and the 41%-vs-25% circuit-breaker threshold are configured values in production-us-east-2 that converted a slow/failing provider into 4xx/5xx customer responses and sustained retry backlog; whether those settings are themselves misconfigured in us-east-2 could not be checked because no us-east-2 ConfigMap or Deployment was readable.

A flagd fault-injection flag such as paymentFailure or paymentUnreachable could in principle reproduce the same payment-service/payment-provider symptoms, but the only flagd config readable (production-eu-west-2) has all flags off and no us-east-2 flagd or feature-flag object was readable, so injection in the incident stack remains unverified rather than supported or excluded.

Confirm with the payment provider's own status/incident record whether stripe-us was degraded on 2026-11-23 between roughly 15:20Z and 17:20Z, and compare with the internal 30s timeout and 25% breaker threshold before changing either.

Collect production-us-east-2 pod status, restart counts, events, checkout/payment ConfigMaps and the us-east-2 flagd flag file, and register Prometheus/Jaeger for that target, to corroborate the log chain with error rates and traces.

gaps: Prometheus is unreachable for this target: execute_prometheus_instant_query (twice), get_metric_names, get_all_labels and metrics_range_query all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no error-rate, latency or call-volume series exist for this Run and the ERROR/latency series for checkout-service and payment-service are unknown, not zero.

Jaeger is unreachable: traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE and traces_search for service checkout over 2026-11-23T15:00:00Z-17:23:08Z returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span-level error detail or per-operation failure rate is available.

Kubernetes access covers only production-eu-west-2; no object in production-us-east-2 could be read, so pod status, container restarts, events, ConfigMaps (timeouts, breaker thresholds, retry settings) and flagd flags of the incident cluster are unknown.
The events query across all namespaces on the readable cluster returned no_data with 0 events; that is only 'this query matched nothing' and carries no information about production-us-east-2 events.

The 'Stripe-US degraded mode acknowledged via status page' statement comes from payment-service's own WARN log; no independent provider status source or telemetry was available, and the change_history integration is not configured, so I cannot tell whether or when any provider or timeout/breaker setting changed.

The payment pod log query in the readable cluster returned 0 lines matching err|error|fail|timeout|exception out of 186 lines read; absence of matching lines is not proof the process logged no errors.

The index holds only 10 documents total, so no failure rate, p95 or volume figure for production-us-east-2 can be computed from it, and checkout-service errors seen in logs cannot be tied to specific downstream spans.
next_steps: Obtain the stripe-us provider incident/status record for 2026-11-23 ~15:20Z-17:20Z to confirm the external degradation independently of payment-service's log line.

Read production-us-east-2 checkout-service and payment-service pod status, last termination reasons, events and ConfigMaps (provider timeout, circuit-breaker threshold, retry queue settings) and the us-east-2 flagd flag file to check for any switched-on fault-injection setting.
Enable or repair Prometheus and Jaeger scraping for the production-us-east-2 target so checkout/payment error rates and traces around 14:22Z-17:18Z can corroborate the log evidence.

view.cannot_prove: A document that is not returned is unknown, not proof that nothing was logged: only size documents are shown, and retention, ingest delay and the index pattern can leave gaps. The time field is the writer's timestamp, not necessarily when the event happened. total and aggregations cover only the matched indices inside the query window.

Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
